guideTitle: The Best Adjustable CPU Stands for Getting a PC Off the Floor
metaTitle: Best Adjustable CPU Stands: Width, Height and Wheels (2026)
metaDescription: Adjustable CPU stands differ in what adjusts: width, length or height. We compared eight on adjustment range, wheels, rails and build to fit your tower and desk.
introParagraphs: A CPU stand lifts a desktop tower off the floor, which can help keep dust and carpet away from the intake vents and makes the PC easier to roll out for cleaning or cable changes. "Adjustable" usually means the width expands to grip the case; a few also adjust length or height.
Measure your tower's width and depth before comparing. Width ranges here run from about 6.3 to 11.8 inches, and at least one stand adjusts height to sit a tower closer to a standing desk.
Most stands here have four swivel casters, and several include side rails. Our comparison is based on published dimensions and features, not hands-on testing.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-1.summary: A metal stand adjusting from 7.87 to 10.23 inches wide, 16.9 inches long, with side rails and wheels.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-1.description:
The Hovadova is the simple, low-cost choice: a metal stand whose width adjusts from 7.87 to 10.23 inches, 16.9 inches long, with protective rails on both sides, a ventilated base and wheels.

Its 16.9-inch length is shorter than some stands here, so check it against a deeper full-tower case.
cons: Capacity not stated in the summary
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-1.bestFor: Standard mid-tower cases on a budget.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-1.skipIf: Your case is long or wide; the AGPTEK adjusts length and width further.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-2.summary: A steel rolling stand whose height adjusts from 5.2 to 11.9 inches, for mid-towers.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-2.description:
The PUTORSEN adjusts height, from 5.2 to 11.9 inches, which lets you raise a mid-tower closer to a sit-stand desk or lift it well off the carpet. It is steel and needs no drilling.

It costs more than the width-only stands, and PUTORSEN lists it for most mid-towers; check full-tower fit.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-2.bestFor: Raising a tower higher off the floor or nearer a sit-stand desk.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-2.skipIf: You only need the tower off the carpet; a width-adjustable stand costs less.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-3.summary: A stand 19.29 inches long, adjusting 8.07 to 10.63 inches wide, with two locking casters.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-3.description:
This stand suits bigger cases: its 19.29-inch length and 8.07- to 10.63-inch width are designed for standard and gaming PC cases, with a ventilated base.

It has four 360-degree casters, two of which lock, so it can be fixed in place. The brand isn't named in the listing.
cons: Capacity not stated in the summary
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-3.bestFor: Gaming or full-size cases that need a longer base.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-3.skipIf: You want length adjustment too; the AGPTEK adjustable stand offers it.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-4.summary: An adjustable rolling stand with side rails and four 360-degree wheels.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-4.description:
This stand covers the basics: side rails to keep the case from slipping off and four 360-degree wheels so you can roll the tower out to clean.

The listing summary doesn't give its width range or dimensions, so check them against your case before buying.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-4.bestFor: A basic rolling platform for a standard case.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-4.skipIf: You want stated dimensions; the Hovadova lists its range.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-5.summary: An AGPTEK stand adjusting 6.3 to 11.8 inches wide and 15.7 to 20 inches long.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-5.description:
The AGPTEK adjustable stand has the widest ranges here: 6.3 to 11.8 inches wide and 15.7 to 20 inches long, so it can fit a slim case or a large tower.

It rolls on four 360-degree casters. Its price sits in the middle of this guide at the time of writing.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-5.bestFor: Unusual case sizes, or a stand that may move to a new PC later.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-5.skipIf: Your case is a standard mid-tower; the Hovadova costs less.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-6.summary: A walnut-finish wood and PVC stand with lockable wheels and a ventilated platform.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-6.description:
The fulkun is the stand to choose if it will be visible: wood pieces with PVC in a walnut finish, with a ventilated platform and four universal wheels that lock.

fulkun describes it as having greater load-bearing capacity, but the listing summary doesn't give a figure or dimensions.
cons: Wood less tolerant of damp floors
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-6.bestFor: A tower in view in a living space.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-6.skipIf: Looks don't matter; the metal stands cost less.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-7.summary: EUREKA ERGONOMIC's height-adjustable two-tier PC cart with quiet wheels for carpet.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-7.description:
The EUREKA ERGONOMIC stand is a two-tier cart rather than a simple platform: height-adjustable, with a second shelf for a UPS, router or storage, and four 360-degree wheels described as quiet and suited to carpet.

It was the most expensive stand here at the time of writing, several times the price of the basic stands.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-7.bestFor: A tower plus UPS or router on one rolling cart.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-7.skipIf: You only need to lift the tower; any basic stand does that for far less.

best-adjustable-cpu-stands-8.summary: AGPTEK's basic steel rolling CPU stand with four upgraded wheels.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-8.description:
The AGPTEK CPU Stand is the least expensive option here: a steel rolling stand with four wheels AGPTEK describes as upgraded.

The listing summary doesn't state an adjustment range or dimensions, so confirm it fits your case.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-8.bestFor: The simplest, cheapest way to get a tower off the floor.
best-adjustable-cpu-stands-8.skipIf: You need a wide range; the AGPTEK adjustable model fits more cases.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Compare your tower's width and depth with the stand's range. Widths here run from about 6.3 to 11.8 inches; lengths from 15.7 to 20 inches.
Most stands adjust width; the AGPTEK adjustable adds length; the PUTORSEN and EUREKA adjust height.
Locking casters keep the tower from drifting; several listings here don't mention locks.
Side rails help stop a case from sliding off when rolled.

faq.a: It lifts the tower off the floor, which can reduce dust and carpet fibers near the intake, and lets you roll it out for cleaning.
Compare your case's width and depth with the stand's listed range.
They help stop the stand drifting, especially on hard floors. The 19.29-inch stand and fulkun list them.
Width fits the case; height raises it further, which helps with sit-stand desks.
Most listings here don't state a capacity; check before loading a heavy full tower.

bottomLine: For a standard mid-tower, the Hovadova is the low-cost choice with side rails, and the AGPTEK adjustable stand fits the widest range of cases. For long gaming cases, the 19.29-inch stand adds locking casters.
If you want height, the PUTORSEN raises the tower up to 11.9 inches, and the EUREKA two-tier cart adds a shelf for more money. The fulkun suits a visible spot.
